items.student_text: A rectangle has side lengths $x+3$ and $x+4$. Use the area model to explain how the four partial areas combine into one polynomial for total area. Then describe what must change if one side becomes $x-2$ instead.
items.student_html: A rectangle has side lengths $x+3$ and $x+4$. Use the area model to explain how the four partial areas combine into one polynomial for total area. Then describe what must change if one side becomes $x-2$ instead.
items.answer_text: The partial areas are $x^2,4x,3x,12$, so total area is $x^2+7x+12$. Replacing $x+3$ by $x-2$ makes the second row negative: $-2x$ and $-8$, changing the product to $x^2+2x-8$.

items.expected_evidence: The partial areas are $x^2,4x,3x,12$, so total area is $x^2+7x+12$. Replacing $x+3$ by $x-2$ makes the second row negative: $-2x$ and $-8$, changing the product to $x^2+2x-8$.
